slides.0.title: Coteaux d'Aix, Les Baux and Coteaux Varois
slides.0.subtitle: Coteaux d'Aix-en-Provence in the west, Les Baux-de-Provence in the Alpilles and inland Coteaux Varois
slides.1.title: Coteaux d'Aix-en-Provence
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Area and history
slides.1.highlights.0.content: AOC by decree of 24 December 1985 (VDQS in 1956); INAO lists 49 communes: 47 in Bouches-du-Rhône and 2 in Var (Artigues and Rians) (INAO, Wine With Seth)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Rules
slides.1.highlights.1.content: INAO: red and rosé principals are Cinsault, Counoise, Grenache, Mourvèdre and Syrah with Grenache at least 20%; white needs at least 50% Vermentino; yield 60 hl/ha; Cabernet Sauvignon is accessory (introduced in the 1960s, Wikipedia)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Soils and colour mix
slides.1.highlights.2.content: INAO: stony clay-loam on marl gives alcoholic, structured wines; sandy soils on molasse and sandstone give lighter, fruitier wines. CIVP 2025: 216,459 hl, rosé 182,412 hl (about 84%); older sources give different colour splits, so this is not tested
slides.1.content: The hills around Aix are Provence's western gateway.
slides.2.title: Les Baux-de-Provence
slides.2.highlights.0.title: A small Alpilles appellation
slides.2.highlights.0.content: AOC recognised on 20 April 1995; the INAO specification lists 7 communes (Les Baux-de-Provence, Fontvieille, Maussane-les-Alpilles, Mouriès, Paradou, Saint-Étienne-du-Grès, Saint-Rémy-de-Provence); about 300 ha (Wine With Seth; another page says 8 communes, but INAO's 7 is followed)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Rules
slides.2.highlights.1.content: INAO (draft revision): principal varieties together at least 60% and each at most 90%; Cabernet Sauvignon in red at most 20%; yield 50 hl/ha; herbicides banned; red aged until 15 September of the year after harvest
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Organic and Trévallon
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Wine With Seth says the appellation is fully organic from the 2023 vintage, but the INAO text only bans herbicides, so this is flagged and not tested; Domaine de Trévallon bottles as IGP Alpilles after refusing the 20% Cabernet cap in 1993 (Wine With Seth)
slides.2.content: A small, strict appellation, and one that a famous estate chose to leave.
slides.3.title: Coteaux Varois en Provence
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Inland Provence Verte
slides.3.highlights.0.content: INAO: 28 communes in the Var; vineyards average about 350 m and reach about 500 m; enclosed by massifs such as the Sainte-Baume, with continental influence (CIVP 2019 press kit)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Timeline
slides.3.highlights.1.content: The name Coteaux varois appeared in 1945, vin de pays in 1974, VDQS in 1984, AOC in 1993 and the rename to Coteaux varois en Provence in 2005; it is the youngest of the three main Vins de Provence AOCs
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Style and colour
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Cooler, higher sites give good acidity and structure (Wine Folly); white leans on Rolle at least 30% (CIVP press kit); the rosé share ranges from 82% to 92% by source (INAO page 90%, press kit 92%, CIVP 2025 about 82%), so it is not tested
slides.3.content: Inland altitude makes the rosé tighter than on the coast.
